title: Scalar comparison of vector integration counits
statement: For an independently integration-normalized vector purity family, the full prescribed scalar-reduction compatibility law holds, with the canonical source comparison and actual exceptional mate. This is one compatibility clause, not the vector-bundle purity theorem.

source.place: paragraph 2; assembly step 5, normalized transpose in the published vector-purity coordinates

proof.text:
Map the annihilator equation through phi. Use the uniquely pure-root-normalized finite Tate
balancing and its ordered shifted tensor powers. Its source maps are invertible, including nonflat
coefficient extensions. Compact-support scalar coherence makes the actual compact comparison
invertible. Scalar trace descent and projection coherence identify the integration counits.
Transpose their equality, using the inverse of this compact comparison; its adjunct is the
published scalar mate. Since both purity families and the source comparison are invertible, so is
the scalar mate. The same equation at the coefficient unit gives the required unit compatibility.
Rank zero uses the unit maps; empty schemes have unique maps.

proof_origin.place: paragraph 2; the independent scalar-reduction portion of vector-bundle purity
